title: Connect to a Wi-Fi network using iwctl
summary: Use the iwctl command-line tool to scan for and connect to a Wi-Fi network. This assumes iwd is already installed and running.
prerequisites: User is in the 'network' or 'wheel' group, or using sudo

alternatives.explain: Connect to the specified Wi-Fi network. If the network is secured, you will be prompted to enter the password.

placeholders.name: STATION
placeholders.description: The name of your Wi-Fi interface, e.g., wlan0 or phy0

placeholders.name: NETWORK_NAME
placeholders.description: The name (SSID) of the Wi-Fi network you want to connect to

steps.explain: List available Wi-Fi devices to find your device name (e.g., wlan0).
steps.expect: A list of devices is shown.

steps.explain: Scan for available networks using your device name.

placeholders.name: DEVICE_NAME
placeholders.description: Your Wi-Fi interface name, e.g., wlan0

steps.explain: List the scanned networks to find the SSID you want to connect to.
Connect to the chosen network. You will be prompted for the password if required.

placeholders.name: SSID
placeholders.description: The name of the Wi-Fi network

steps.expect: Connection established or password prompt appears.

verify.expect: State is 'connected' and SSID is shown.
